snippet: Following the destruction of the Bed of Chaos, Quelana appears to have returned to Izalith, or what remains of it, at some point. title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : __NOTOC__

There are four **endings to *Dark Souls III***.

All four endings require the Ashen One to first gather the cinders of four great lords to reach the Kiln of the First Flame, where they must defeat the Soul of Cinder. Only the first ending does not require actions beyond strictly the main questline, although it is possible for up to three to be available simultaneously at the Kiln. All endings revolve around the First Flame, symbolized by a special bonfire that can be interacted with upon slaying the Soul of Cinder.

snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

 soul_of_cinder : After returning to the shrine, the Ashen One places the ashes of the Lords on their thrones, and the Firekeeper channels their strength to the Ashen One. The Firekeeper bids the Ashen One travel to the First Flame. Accepting the strength of the Lords, the Ashen One is transported to a copy of the Firelink shrine, standing amid the wreckage of kingdoms. From there, the Ashen One proceeds to the Kiln of the First Flame.

There they encounter the Soul of Cinder, a manifestation of the Lords that had previously linked the flame. The Soul of Cinder takes on many forms and fighting styles, mimicking those who had linked the flame. Once the Ashen One weakens it, the Soul of Cinder assumes the style of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, first one to link the flame. title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

 lore : The Lords of Cinder are beings that have linked the First Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire through the centuries. Although many of these champions have followed the sacrifice of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, not everyone became a Lord of Cinder through heroic deeds or even of free will. One such case is Aldrich, who became a Lord only because he had the strength to become one, despite having obtained such power by devouring an untold number of humans for his own pleasure.

The continuous linking of the Flame eventually culminated in the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who linked the Flame throughout history. This being, although appearing as an empty husk, inherits the abilities of the Lords of Cinders who have come before. It has long existed as the Flame's last defense inside the Kiln, protecting it from Champions attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: He gathered an army of deacons, who cast off their red robes and crowns—symbolic of their clerical duties— for new dark-blue ones and swore fealty as Aldrich Faithful, their venerance of the Deep finally codified under Aldrich's banner. He then marched on Irithyll, home to the old gods of Anor Londo and the residence of Chief Deity Gwyndolin. From the battle that ensued, Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and forcing him into capitulation. Seemingly, the two eventually struck a deal: the Pontiff would maintain some control over lower Irithyll; in exchange, Aldrich would be granted access to Gwyndolin, who was imprisoned by the Pontiff within the old Cathedral of Anor Londo.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At his new posting at the Cathedral, Aldrich was provided a steady flow of sustenance in the form of the Road of Sacrifices. The Cathedral would dispatch Evangelists to establish missions and gain influence at the Undead Settlement; these preachers would tell stories of enlightenment to the cursed Undead, who were shipped off en masse to become feed to Aldrich's gluttony. The bearers of these rings underwent a mutation similar to his, transforming into bestial creatures with stomachs filled with the remains of their meals and infused with the power of the Deep.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their very essence, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder just for his strength, without any consideration for his morality or how he acquired his power. Now left to indulge in his every perversion so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : At the beginning of the fight, charge at Aldrich to avoid his hard-hitting soul spear. Get behind him and focus your attacks on his tail. This leaves him with nothing to do but swing his two slow, devastating melee attacks or teleport across the room (usually, adjacent to where he teleported from).

At about 55%-60% health, he will teleport and come back up, buffed with fire. His arrows also go from going forward to following a specific player. If the arrows following the player catch up to them, then that player will most likely go down quick. Blue Bug and Red Bug Pellets are recommended for this fight.

Casting the sorcery Twisted Wall of Light can negate Aldrich's ranged attacks, including his arrow barrage in the second phase, allowing one to wait out the attack by casting repeatedly.

Before eating Gwyndolin, Aldrich imposed on himself a practice of asceticism (苦行), that is, he refrained from eating humans before he could devour the god.
During the fight, as well as when the boss is passive, shrieks and moans of pain can be heard coming from Gwyndolin. title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At one point, Sulyvahn sent McDonnell, an Archdeacon from Irithyll that was a sorcerer despite being a high-ranking cleric, to help the deacons of the Cathedral. McDonnell shared his sorceries with the priests of the Cathedral, who in turn became sorcerers, turning their holy candles into sorcery staves and blades, better equipped to face the abominations of the Deep. However McDonnell would soon find delight in the stagnant souls of the Deep, believing the place to be the "bottom of the world". Over time the deacons themselves, despite their faith and holy flame, began to succumb to the power of the Deep. They began to add dark stories about the Deep to the holy scriptures intended to grant them divine protection, corrupting these holy tales into profanity. McDonnell realized that the rotten darkness of the Deep could become an incredible new power, and by studying it, he created sorceries that manipulated the dark soul dregs, then imparted them to Archdeacon Royce and his deacons.

 lead : The **Ashen One,** also referred to as the **Champion of Ash** or **the Unkindled One,** is the playable character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls III*.

The title of Ashen One is given to the player by the Fire Keeper of Firelink Shrine. The Ashen One is an Unkindled, an Undead who failed to link the First Flame and became ash, who has been raised from their grave, and is tasked with a journey to defeat four Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, since the link of the Flame is threatened and the Lords refuse to serve as its fuel once again.

 irithyll_and_anor_londo_dark_souls_iii_anor_londo : On the surface, the Ashen One fights their way to the grand church in Irithyll where they find Pontiff Sulyvahn. Killing Sulyvahn opens the way to Anor Londo, fabled city of the gods, where Aldrich awaits. Aldrich, having lost interest in the flame and having instead turned towards the Dark, sought out Anor Londo to devour the gods themselves. He found and devoured Dark Sun Gwyndolin in Anor Londo, who had been "stricken by illness" and had retreated to the Anor Londo Cathedral, only to be imprisoned by the Pontiff to be fed to Aldrich. Fighting their way past the archers protecting the city, the Ashen One finds Aldrich using Gwyndolin as a puppet of sorts, and kills him, acquiring his ashes to be delivered to his throne.

One is a gesture that will allow passage to Archdragon Peak, and the other is a secret path to the Untended Graves, a dark version of Firelink Shrine. Here the Ashen One finds Champion Gundyr, and behind him an abandoned Firelink Shrine home only to a Shrine Handmaiden. Here the Ashen One can find the Eyes of a Fire Keeper which if presented to the Firekeeper will allow her to see a dark vision of the future that the Ashen One may choose to fulfill.

In Archdragon Peak, the Ashen One can face the Ancient Wyvern and The Nameless King, once known as Lord Gwyn's Firstborn, the old God of War who aligned himself with the Ancient Dragons.

title: Ashen One
snippet: After defeating Halflight, the path to Filianore is open. Filianore lies sleeping while clutching a broken egg-like object. If the Ashen One touches the object, it will shatter into pieces and Filianore will wake, upon which a blinding light emanates from the shards of the object and envelopes the chamber. The Ashen One opens their eyes to find that the Ringed City is now a lifeless desert, and Filianore an emaciated corpse. Leaving her room, the Ashen One comes upon a fleeing Pygmy. Investigating the scene closer, they find Gael consuming the remains of a Pygmy Lord in order to gain their Dark Soul. He proceeds to attack the Ashen One in order to gain their piece of the Dark Soul.

 cemetery_of_ash : At some point in time, the Ashen One attempted to link the fire. They were not powerful enough and were instead burnt to ash by the flames. The Ashen One emerges from their grave and sets out to leave their tomb. Finding the Coiled Sword lodged inside Iudex Gundyr, the Ashen One pulls it out, awakening Gundyr and beginning a fight. Halfway through, Gundyr is seemingly consumed by the Pus of Man, but the Ashen One defeats him and finds Firelink Shrine.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - catacombs_of_carthus 
 catacombs_of_carthus : Progressing through the trap-ridden Catacombs, the Ashen One eventually finds a rickety drawbridge that will lead them to Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Should the Ashen One choose to descend the fallen drawbridge, they may find the Smouldering Lake, ruled by the Old Demon King and home to various demons and a great slithering worm.

Across the bridge, the Ashen One finds a strange goblet that pulls them into the Abyss. Here they encounter High Lord Wolnir, who attacks the Ashen One. By destroying his enchanted bracelets, Wolnir loses his grip and falls into the Abyss, allowing the Ashen One to return to the regular world, where the path to Irithyll, a frozen city guarded by an impenetrable barrier and ruled by Pontiff Sulyvahn in the name of Aldrich, is now open.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Deep within the Cathedral, the Ashen One encounters the Deacons of the Deep guarding Aldrich's tomb. After defeating them, the Ashen One finds that Aldrich has left the cathedral, finding instead a doll that will allow the Ashen One to enter Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

After returning to Firelink Shrine, the Ashen One again encounters Anri and Horace, who tell the Ashen One that Aldrich supposedly hails from Irithyll and that he may have returned home. They will also find Sirris of the Sunless Realms, who shows little interest in the Ashen One, unless they provide the Handmaiden with a certain ash, prompting Sirris to offer the Ashen One her sign.

title: Ashen One

They may then return this to the Painter, who states that she will use the Blood of the Dark Soul to paint a new Painted World. She offers to name it after the Ashen One, and if the Ashen One gives no name, she states that she will name it the Painted World of Ash.

title: Ashen One
snippet: At this point in the game, Yoel of Londor will die. If the Ashen One has allowed him to draw out their true strength a sufficient number of times, Yoel will be replaced by Yuria of Londor, who attempts to sway the Ashen One into usurping the First Flame and becoming the Lord of Hollows.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
***Ash Seeketh Embers**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. Before the flames fade, the Ashen One may strike her down. The Ashen One steps over the limp body of the Fire Keeper and takes the First Flame into their own hands. Kneeling, the Ashen One raises the flame, offering it to the Darksign Sun.
***The Usurpation of Fire**: If the Ashen One allowed Yoel to draw out their true strength a sufficient amount of times through the Dark Sigil, followed Yuria's instructions and "married" Anri, the Ashen One may, instead of linking the fire, absorb it into themselves. The Ashen One collapses from the strain and awakens before a Darksign Sun turned white, and also finds Yuria, Anri, and an army of hollows greeting them as their Lord and praying for the Ashen One to make Londor whole.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - road_of_sacrifices_and_crucifixion_woods 
 road_of_sacrifices_and_crucifixion_woods : Following the road leads the Ashen One to the Crucifixion Woods, where they encounter Anri of Astora and their companion Horace the Hushed. Anri seeks Aldrich, and thinks to find him in the Cathedral of the Deep. They offer their help to the Ashen One, should the Ashen One need it. Here the Ashen One may also find Orbeck of Vinheim, a sorcerer who will offer to share his knowledge if the Ashen One brings him magic scrolls.

Making their way through the Crucifixion Woods leads the Ashen One to a crossroads. One path leads to Farron Keep, home of the Abyss Watchers, whereas the other one, guarded by one of the Crystal Sages, leads to the Cathedral of the Deep, home of Aldrich.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - the_painted_world_of_ariandel 
 the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - undead_settlement 
 undead_settlement : Arriving in the Undead Settlement, the Ashen One finds Yoel of Londor praying for death at a ledge. Upon encountering the Ashen One, Yoel offers his services, providing rudimentary sorceries and offering to draw out the Ashen One's "true strength", not telling them that doing so will burden the Ashen One with the Dark Sigil which will make them hollow upon death.

Inside the Settlement, the Ashen One is accosted by the inhabitants of the town and pelted with massive arrows by a Giant atop a tower. After fighting and killing the Curse-rotted Greatwood, the Ashen One will find a Transposing Kiln that will allow Ludleth to provide great spells and weapons from the souls of powerful creatures.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - grand_archives_and_prince_lothric 
 grand_archives_and_prince_lothric : Progressing through Lothric Castle will bring the Ashen One face to face with a Dragonslayer Armour controlled by a Pilgrim Butterfly. Defeating the armour opens the way to the Grand Archives, home to ancient knowledge.

The Ashen One fights their way through the Archives, and find themselves close to the location of Prince Lothric, who hides at the very top of the castle. Lothric has no intention of returning as a Lord of Cinder however, preferring to watch the world end from afar with his brother Lorian. The brothers attack the Ashen One, who slays them both, and claims Lothric's ashes.

title: Ashen One

Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : The Ashen One, as depicted in promotional material, is a Knight.
The Ashen One is often referred to as the 'Champion of Ash' or the 'Unkindled One' by other characters.
A knight in the cover is named as 'Red Knight' in the Funko Pop! line.
**There’s a misconception about the Soul of Cinder armor and the Red Knight armor: They are essentially the same Firelink set, the only difference being that the Red Knight (Ashen One) version has a tabard, while the Soul of Cinder version does not.
**The Red Knight armor is a variant of the Firelink set, distinguished by its tabard bearing a coat of arms reminiscent of the Lothric Knights.
In the Pre-Alpha *Dark Souls III*, the Ashen One is shown to use a cut-content weapon called the Legion Scimitars. Its dual combat art Spin Slash was ultimately given to the Sellsword Twinblades, while its design was relegated to a curved sword named Scimitar.

 profaned_capital : Descending through the dungeon of Irithyll brings the Ashen One to the Profaned Capital, home of the reclusive Yhorm the Giant, one of the missing lords. Fighting their way past the gargoyles and priestesses that guard the way to the giant, the Ashen One finds him atop his throne. The enormously strong and durable Yhorm initially seems insurmountable, but the Ashen One finds the magic blade Storm Ruler, a sword with the ability to fell giants, beside his throne. Using the power of the blade, the Ashen One is able to bring Yhorm to his knees and kill him, collecting his ashes.

title: Ashen One

 the_ringed_city : If the Ashen One follows Gael, they will find themselves in the Dreg Heap, an amalgamation of collapsed kingdoms and civilizations at the end of time. Within the Dreg Heap they may encounter Lapp, a hollow who seeks the Purging Monument in order to remember his past life. Fighting their way past the Dreg Heap they find two demons, the Demon in Pain & the Demon Below. Following the fall of the last of the two, its corpse is enkindled by the Chaos Flame and reawakened as the Demon Prince. Defeating the Demon Prince allows the Ashen One to travel to the Ringed City, the first city of Man, inhabited by the Pygmies. Gwyn, the first Lord of Cinder, had gifted the city to humanity after the end of the Age of Ancients, along with his daughter Filianore.

 irithyll_of_the_boreal_valley : The Ashen One is able to penetrate the barrier to Irithyll with the magic doll they found in the Cathedral of the Deep. Progressing through the frozen city, the Ashen One will again come to a crossroads. They may either descend through the dungeons of Irithyll to find the Profaned Capital, or progress further into the city, finding the ancient city of the gods, Anor Londo.

 cathedral_of_the_deep : After defeating the Crystal Sage, the Ashen One follows the road to the Cathedral of the Deep. Once there, the Ashen One may encounter a "knight of Catarina" who will attempt to lure them onto a narrow path with the promises of treasure. Should the Ashen One fail to see through his ruse, the "knight" will lower them below where a giant awaits before revealing himself to be Unbreakable Patches, a thief and con-artist. If confronted later, Patches will attempt to feign innocence, but if the Ashen One presses him on the matter, he will admit his wrongdoings and offer a gift in recompense, as well as selling the Ashen One his goods.

title: Ashen One
snippet: ***The End of Fire**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. She states that the fire quickly fades and that dark will soon settle, but predicts that one day, tiny flames will dance across the darkness, like embers linked by lords past, suggesting that the other Lords of Cinder of the past will one day rise and wander through the darkness with their own fragments of the First Flame. As the absolute darkness settles upon the world, the Fire Keeper asks if the Ashen One can still hear her.

title: Ashen One

 returning_to_the_high_wall : After slaying the penultimate Lord of Cinder, the Ashen One is transported back to Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle in the High Wall of Lothric. A dying Emma begs the Ashen One to find Prince Lothric and tell him that he must be a Lord of Cinder, giving the Ashen One the Basin of Vows that will allow them access into Lothric Castle.

Before the Ashen One can place the basin, they are ambushed by the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, who attacks them. After killing the Dancer, the Ashen One can place the basin and gain access to the castle.

The king, having gone mad long ago and deformed himself into a dragon-like being, ferociously attacks the Ashen One.

 high_wall_of_lothric : The Ashen One then progresses through the High Wall of Lothric, now home to mindless hollow soldiers, knights, and a fire-breathing wyvern. Fighting their way to a church, they encounter Emma, the high priestess of Lothric Castle. Emma provides them with a banner that will allow them safe passage to the Undead Settlement, but warns them that their path is guarded by Vordt of the Boreal Valley. title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - quelaag_s_domain_bell 
 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The Bells of Awakening are hinted at being the first destination of the Chosen Undead and, when rung, the fate of the undead shall be known. Upon arriving in Firelink Shrine, the Crestfallen Warrior informs the player that there are, in fact, two Bells of Awakening. One up above and one far below. This is essentially all the instruction and plot that is revealed upon arrival in Lordran.

title: Bells of Awakening

snippet: Greeting their new Lord are Yuria and her sister Liliane of the Sable Church of Londor, who kneel in veneration. title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The following steps are required:
Meet and recruit Yoel of Londor at the Undead Settlement; after he relocates to Firelink Shrine, allow him to "Draw out True Strength" five times to receive one Dark Sigil every time. This must only be done before the player enters the Catacombs of Carthus after defeating the Abyss Watchers.
** Every time the player dies, hollowing points equal to the amount of sigils gained are accrued.
** One sigil is available the moment Yoel arrives at the Shrine. The remaining 4 sigils are given at or above 2, 6, 12, and 18 hollowing respectively. Dying twice after each sigil gained will accrue enough hollowing to gain the next. As long as the player does not enter the Catacombs, there are no time constraints regarding when to recruit Yoel or acquire the Sigils.
Meet Anri and Horace at the Road of Sacrifices and exhaust dialogue between both characters.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Also of note regarding this questline:
** Giving the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper does not void the questline; if they did so, the player must however avoid summoning her using the sign next to the First Flame bonfire, as doing so will lead to another ending.
** Although it is not recommended as there are no benefits, it is actually fine to kill Yoel after obtaining five Sigils from him; he welcomes this death, and Yuria's dialogue is unaffected.
** Although Yuria requests of the Ashen One to kill Orbeck of Vinheim if he has arrived in the Shrine, this is unrelated to the questline and not necessary to this ending.
** Unlike the other two Pilgrims, the Stone-humped Hag atop The Dreg Heap is unrelated to the questline and can be killed freely without consequences.
** If the questline is being followed, the Londor Pale Shades will be available as summonable phantoms throughout the game; if the quest has been voided, they will invade as Dark Spirits instead.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Must their Dark Sigils with the Fire Keeper after she receives the Fire Keeper Soul (the player Purging Stones or "Request Dissolution" at either the Shrine of Velka in the Undead Settlement or the Purging Monument in The Ringed City); doing so will be perceived as a betrayal by Yuria, leading her to either never appear or rebuke the Ashen One upon their next interaction.
Must not proceed into the Catacombs of Carthus before acquiring 5 Dark Sigils (defeating the Abyss Watchers or interacting with the bonfire which spawns upon their defeat before acquiring the Sigils does not void the questline, but is not recommended in order to avoid accidents).

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:

title: Soul Appease
snippet:
Soul Appease -  Dark Souls II - spell - general_information 
 general_information : When cast, Soul Appease releases a yellow ring around the caster, dealing damage within a large area-of-effect. It can hit through walls and deals considerable damage, but only to specific enemies. However, its area of effect is vaguely dome-shaped, meaning that while it is capable of hitting enemies above the caster, if an enemy is on an even slightly lower level than them it will miss them altogether.

Although situational, Soul Appease is an effective way of clearing mobs of enemies affected by it. However, the fickle nature of what the spell considers undead can make it difficult to tell when the spell can be used.

title: Bluemoon Greatsword

 description : The blade of this greatsword shines like the brilliant rays of the moon. In the oldest legends, rarely spoken of today, it is said that the sword was born of a great white being.

Then, what explains this lifeless weapon?
Perhaps there has been some mistake...
